title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 20-22). Grothendieck studies 'Dedekind-Azumaya categories' C over a Dedekind ring A with fraction field K. These are A-linear categories in which each D = End(X) is an order in a central simple K-algebra E = D⊗_A K, Azumaya over an open U of Spec A. The previous page shows such a C is the same as a G_m-gerbe G (with a rank function n(x)) whose degree-1 representations of locally given rank recover C. Extending scalars to A' (on the next page A' = ∏_{ℓ≠p} Z_ℓ), C_{A'} is the representation category of the gerbe G_{A'}.

This page asks when there are CANONICAL invertible objects, i.e. a canonical neutralisation of the determinant gerbe. The plan is to build a transitive system of isomorphisms between the det(X_{A'}) for X in ob C. Since every other object is X' = P⊗_D X with P an invertible right D-module (D = End X), and det(P⊗X) ≅ N_red(P)·det X (previous page), it suffices to give a canonical isomorphism (*) det P = N_red(P) ≅ A satisfying three conditions:
(i) It is functorial in P. Automorphisms of P are the units of the commutant D' = End_D(P), so this forces N_red(D'^*) = {1}.
(ii) It is compatible with passage to the commutant.
(iii) It is multiplicative for Q⊗_{D'}P, i.e. N_red(Q⊗_{D'}P, D) ≅ N_red(Q, D')⊗N_red(P, D), compatibly with the given isomorphisms.

Set Φ = N_red(E^*) ⊂ K^*. Sufficient conditions are:
- Pic(A) = 0, so the invertible A-module N_red(P) is a principal fractional ideal qA;
- Φ ∩ A^* = {1} and Φ·A^* = K^*, so the generator q can be chosen uniquely inside Φ.
The trivialisation is then 'the unique generator lying in Φ'. Units have norm in Φ ∩ A^* = 1, giving functoriality, and multiplicativity follows because Φ is a group.

Example: A = Z and E_R = E⊗R not split, i.e. E a definite quaternion algebra over Q. By the Hasse-Schilling-Maass norm theorem Φ = Q_{>0}, so Φ ∩ {±1} = {1} and Φ·{±1} = Q^*. Hence Rep(G_{A'}) has a canonical invertible object of degree 1, and the gerbe's structural data trivialise.

Purpose (next page): C = supersingular elliptic curves in characteristic p, a 'Deuring category'. The relevant E is the quaternion algebra ramified exactly at p and ∞, and the gerbe lives over Z[1/p]. Tate modules give a fibre functor over A' = ∏_{ℓ≠p} Z_ℓ, and the canonical determinant should match A'(1) via the Weil pairing. Positivity of reduced norms here is just positivity of isogeny degrees.
errors: The written condition 'N_red: D^* → A^* à valeurs dans 1' should read 'with values in {1}'. As applied, it is needed for the commutant orders D' = End(P), not only for D. For A = Z and a definite quaternion order it holds, since unit norms are positive units, hence 1.

Uniqueness of the canonical isomorphism also implicitly uses that the reduced norm of an invertible D-module is computed inside E and lands in a principal ideal generated by an element of Φ. This is fine for A = Z (Hasse-Schilling-Maass, Eichler), but the general sufficiency claim is only sketched ('Cela marche si on suppose ...'). It is not proved, and the compatibility with commutants is left as '....'.
The condition 'Φ·A^* = K^*' is stronger than needed: it suffices that every reduced-norm ideal has a generator in Φ. This is harmless.

ideas.what: Classification of A-linear categories whose endomorphism rings are orders in central simple algebras via G_m-gerbes over Spec A (twisted sheaves / Azumaya algebras)
ideas.modern_name: Brauer group / G_m-gerbes and twisted modules; categories of modules over Azumaya algebras
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Le groupe de Brauer), Giraud (Cohomologie non abélienne, 1971)
ideas.where_published: Le groupe de Brauer I-III (Dix exposés); Giraud's book develops the gerbe language

ideas.what: Canonical trivialisation of reduced-norm (determinant) line bundles using positivity: choose the unique generator of N_red(P) lying in N_red(E^*), when Pic(A)=0, N_red(E^*)∩A^*=1 and N_red(E^*)·A^*=K^*
ideas.modern_name: Positivity of reduced norms for totally definite quaternion algebras (Hasse-Schilling-Maass norm theorem) used as an 'orientation' of determinant gerbes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Norm theorem: Hasse, Schilling, Maass (1930s); Eichler for orders

ideas.what: Viewing supersingular elliptic curves over F̄_p as an integral 'Deuring category' over Z (or Z[1/p]) attached to the quaternion algebra ramified at p and ∞, with an adelic fibre functor given by Tate modules and det ≅ A'(1)
ideas.modern_name: Deuring correspondence as an equivalence of categories (supersingular curves ↔ invertible right modules over a maximal order); Weil pairing; supersingular part of the motivic Galois gerbe over F_p
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deuring (1941); categorical form: Waterhouse (1969), Ribet, Kohel (1996), Jordan-Keeton-Poonen-Rains-Shepherd-Barron-Tate (2018); motivic gerbe: Langlands-Rapoport (1987), Milne

ideas.what: Determinant of an object of a Dedekind-Azumaya category as a representation of the associated gerbe, with det(P⊗X) ≅ N_red(P)·det X
ideas.modern_name: Reduced norm functor on invertible modules (Fröhlich, Reiner 'Maximal Orders'); determinant of a twisted sheaf

missed.claim: The page uses positivity of reduced norms of a definite quaternion algebra to canonically neutralise the determinant of an integral Brauer-type gerbe. This is the algebraic counterpart of the fact that isogeny degrees are positive. Feeding it into the supersingular Deuring category gives a Tannakian/gerbe description over Z[1/p] whose determinant is canonically A'(1). This is an integral, adelic precursor of the supersingular part of the Langlands-Rapoport pseudomotivic groupoid, formulated in 1965 and in gerbe language.
missed.quote: Cela marche si on suppose ... Pic(A)=0, Φ∩A* = {1}, Φ.A* = K* ... si A=Z, E_K (=E_R) pas déployée sur R. Donc dans ce cas, on a un objet inv. canonique de degré 1 de Rep(G_{A'})
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral and adelic versions of motivic Galois gerbes over finite fields are still not fully developed. Here Grothendieck sketches a concrete integral gerbe model of the supersingular isogeny category with a canonical orientation, more than 20 years before Langlands-Rapoport. It is mainly of historical interest, and of mild technical interest for integral Deuring-type equivalences.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is correct and conceptually neat: positivity of quaternion norms orients the determinant gerbe. The ingredients (Deuring, the norm theorem, Weil pairing, Brauer gerbes) are all known. The novelty lies in the early (1965) integral gerbe/Tannakian packaging of the supersingular Deuring category, which anticipates later work but has no clearly new theorem.
transcription_corrections: 'X ∈ 𝒮C' is most likely 'X ∈ ob C'
'de degré ...' at the end → most likely 'de degré 1'
'compatible au commutant des D dans P' – reading plausible; the brackets close a parenthetical begun at '(ce qui suppose ...'
'E_K (=E_R)' – the subscript is probably a place (∞) or K; the meaning is E⊗R
The final sentence fragment 'de sorte que les liens structuraux de la gerbe G_{A'}' presumably continues 'se trivialisent canoniquement' on the next page
The bracket in the margin defines Φ = N_red(E^*) ⊂ K^*, D = End(X), E = D⊗_A K, as transcribed
